key_insight: This paper compares data-assimilated and embedded approaches to learning closure models—components that approximate effects a simulation cannot directly resolve. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish which approach performs better.
problem_solved: Detailed simulations can be too expensive for complex systems or rapid design iterations. Reduced models are faster but need accurate approximations of unresolved dynamics.
method: Use data-driven closure models to approximate missing effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems.
Compare data-assimilated and embedded closure-learning approaches, as indicated by the title.
Specific algorithms, evaluation settings, and quantitative results are not available in the supplied excerpt.
impact: Learning unresolved effects could help practitioners build faster, more accurate scientific simulations. The comparison is relevant to choosing how to combine machine learning with dynamical models, although the excerpt provides no verified performance gains.
